messages.author: ea5016c05fb289b3
messages.subject: determine differences between latent means
parts:
Hi,

I am a newbie in measurement invariance and in lavaan so please pardon me if my question is pretty basic. How to determine differences between latent means after establishing configural, metric, and partial invariance. I have three latent variables and I want to see the difference between two groups per latent variable. Thanks very much.

#import data
UMICS <- read.csv("~/Dropbox/On-going research (September 2013)/U-MICS - Measurement Invariance in R/Measurement Invariance (U-MICS) - December 2013.csv")

#load lavaan
library(lavaan)

#specify the factor structure: com = commitment, exp = exploration, rec = reconsideration of commitment
UMICS.model <- '
  com =~ comP1 + comP2 + comP3
  exp =~ expP1 + expP2 + expP3 
  rec =~ recP1 + recP2 + recP3
  '

###########################################################################
#multiple groups tests begin#

###########################################################################
#LANGUAGE

#semTools command for a series of multiple group models for language invariance
library(semTools)
MI_Language <- measurementInvariance(UMICS.model,
                                     data = UMICS,
                                     group = "Language")

#MODEL 1 configural model
model1_Language <- cfa(UMICS.model,
              data = UMICS,
              group = "Language")
summary(model1_Language, fit.measures = TRUE)

###MODEL 2 weak invariance model - metric invariance
model2_Language <- cfa(UMICS.model,
              data = UMICS,
              group = "Language",
              group.equal = c("loadings"))
summary(model2_Language, fit.measures = TRUE)

#checking the significance of chi-square change in R, model 2 v.s model 1:
anova(model1_Language, model2_Language)

###MODEL 3 strong invariance model - full scalar invariance
model3_Language <- cfa(UMICS.model,
              data = UMICS,
              group = "Language",
              group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts"))
summary(model3_Language, fit.measures = TRUE)

#checking the significance of chi-square change in R, model 3 v.s model 2:
anova(model2_Language, model3_Language)

#strong invariance model-check non-invariant using modification index
modindices(model3_Language)

###MODEL 3a strong invariance model-fit partial invariance mode - partial scalar invariance
model3a_Language <- cfa(UMICS.model,
               data = UMICS,
               group = "Language",
               group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts"),
               group.partial = c("comP3~1", "expP3~1"))
summary(model3a_Language, fit.measures = TRUE)

#checking the significance of chi-square change in R, model 3a v.s model 2:
anova(model2_Language, model3a_Language)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: determine differences between latent means
parts: How to determine differences between latent means after establishing configural, metric, and partial invariance. I have three latent variables and I want to see the difference between two groups per latent variable.

I don't think the measurementInvariance function does partial automatically, so when you fit your strong invariance model, did you free the latent means in the second group?  If not, then constraining the intercepts and latent means across groups simultaneously might be why your strong invariance did not pass.

If your means are free in the second group, after establishing partial strong invariance, then your next step is to constrain the latent means across groups and conduct a chi-sq difference test to see whether that set of constraints is plausible.  To constrain all the latent means (the omnibus test), you can just add "means" to the vector of parameters to constrain in the group.equal argument.  If that test fails, then there are significant group differences in at least one of the latent means.  Instead of constraining all 3 latent means, you can fix one at a time and compare that model to the partial strong invariance model using a chi-sq difference test.  To constrain one at a time, you can either add parameters to the group.partial argument, or you can leave "means" out of the group.equal argument and manual constrain a latent mean using labels in the model syntax (e.g., "com ~ c(mean1, mean1)*com" )

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: determine differences between latent means
parts: I think to constrain a latent mean you have to change the model syntax like this: com ~ c(mean1,mean1)*1

Assuming the means are being estimated to begin with, that would constrain them.  By default, they are fixed to zero, but lavaan does free them in all but the first group when group.equal = "intercepts"
Also I think: adding "means" to the vector "group.partial" does not constrain means to be equal across groups but to be 0 across groups...

"means" is a keyword for group.equal, it does not work in group.partial.  You have to specify individual parameters there, like the original poster did.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

I am also working on this topic, but in my case,  I want to constrain the latent means of one factor, say "com" in this case, to zero in all groups, while freely estimating the latent means of all other factors (in this case "exp" and "rec") in all but the first group. I can do this by specifying this in the syntax: "comm ~ 0*1" while using this argument in the cfa function: group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts")
However, how can I achieve the same result by using the "group.partial" argument? In tried adding "means" to the group.equal argument (in order to fix the latent means in all groups to zero), while adding this: "group.partial = c(""exp~NA*1, "rec~NA*1"), but it doesn't work (all LV means are still zero in all groups). I also tried to remove the "NA" but to no vail. 
In other words, I want to be able to use the group.partial function to specify what specific factor means to freely estimate in all but the first group, while keeping all other factor means (the ones not included in group.partial) fixed to zero in all groups.
Thanks in advance.
